articles.title: iPhone 11 也有份：苹果 iOS 27.3 开发者预览版 Beta 带来 4 项“待机显示”功能
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，科技媒体 MacRumors 今天（11 月 4 日）发布博文，报道称在今天推送的 iOS 27.3 首个 Beta 开发者预览版中，苹果下放 iPhone Duo 上的多项“待机显示”（StandBy）模式，覆盖 iPhone 11 以及后续机型。IT之家注：“待机显示”可以把手机变成桌面时钟、电子相框，或显示小组件和实时活动的信息屏。此次更新并非首次向旧 iPhone 机型开放“待机显示”模式，主要增加显示内容与个性化选择，将此前在 iPhone Duo 上推出的界面功能带到更多设备。本次功能下放适用于 iPhone 11 等后续机型，主要扩展以下 4 项功能：模拟与数字时钟界面增加颜色及附加信息的自定义选项；照片界面支持选择共享相册；新增日历、天气等界面；同一类型的界面可以创建多个版本，并通过滑动切换。用户由此能够保留不同搭配，切换查看时间、浏览照片和获取日常信息。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，科技媒体 9to5Mac 今天（11 月 4 日）发布博文，报道称苹果宣布向第三方开发者开放 Siri AI 的全新“应用技能”（App Skills），让应用能够指导 Siri 执行更复杂的多步骤任务。相关功能将随 iOS 27.3、macOS 27.3 及同期系统更新推出，目前新版系统仍处于开发者测试阶段。该媒体指出本次 Siri 升级主要扩展应用协调能力，Siri 不仅要理解用户想做什么，还能根据应用提供的技能，调用相应的应用操作并串联执行。相比早期仅支持有限预设模式的 Siri AI，新机制进一步扩大了第三方应用的接入范围，也让复杂请求有了更清晰的执行路径。报道援引开发者文档举例，用户可以要求 Siri“通过某款聊天应用，把我收藏的运动鞋发给我的伴侣”。Siri 随后将查找收藏内容，识别伴侣身份，在通讯录中找到对方，再通过指定应用发送运动鞋信息，串联原本需要切换多个应用完成的操作。另一项变化是，用户在部分场景下不必再明确说出应用名称。例如，当网约车应用的“实时活动”正在运行时，用户提出“更改乘车地址”，Siri 就能结合当前情境，判断请求对应哪款应用。IT之家附上相关截图如下：该媒体解读认为 Siri 正尝试从响应单项指令，迈向协调苹果及第三方应用完成连续任务。不过，上述能力尚未正式面向所有用户推出，实际覆盖范围与体验仍需等待后续版本及应用接入情况验证。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，科技媒体 9to5Mac 今天（11 月 4 日）发布博文，报道称苹果 Fitness+ 推出 Gym Strength 力量训练功能，目前已开放测试。新功能面向健身房及居家训练场景，根据用户的目标、经验、时间安排和可用器材，生成四周渐进式计划，并根据每周记录的训练次数与重量，调整下一周内容。用户可选择训练日期和重点部位，每次安排 5 个或 7 个动作，预计分别耗时 20~30 分钟、45~60 分钟，实际时长取决于个人节奏。计划会推荐动作、组数、次数及重量，并提供教练示范视频，支持从三个角度查看动作。据苹果介绍，该功能涵盖超过 350 个动作、适配 30 多类力量训练器材，最低只需配备哑铃。遇到器械被占用或更换场地时，用户可替换器材、选择相近动作，也能增加组数或跳过动作。设备方面，该功能要求 iOS 27.3 或 iPadOS 27.3；搭配 watchOS 27.3，可在 Apple Watch 上查看动作、记录次数和重量。可选的 Training Note 功能由 Apple Intelligence 驱动，提供训练预览、进阶说明及里程碑提示，但要求设备支持苹果智能并设为英语。Gym Strength 纳入现有 Fitness+ 订阅，无需另行付费。美国区订阅价格为每月 9.99 美元（现汇率约合 66.6 元人民币）或每年 79.99 美元（现汇率约合 533.2 元人民币）。IT之家注：苹果 Fitness+ 是苹果推出的付费健身订阅服务，目前暂未在中国大陆上线。用户可以把它理解为“苹果设备里的线上健身课程库”：由教练带领训练，配合音乐、个性化课程推荐和运动数据展示，既能在家跟练，也能在健身房使用。

articles.title: 苹果 watchOS 27.3 首个开发者预览版 Beta 上线音频智能功能：支持全天谈话划重点 / 回顾 15 秒对话
articles.content: IT 之家 11 月 4 日消息，苹果公司今天（11 月 4 日）面向开发者，推送 watchOS 27.3 首个开发者测试版，为 Apple Watch Series 12 和 Apple Watch Ultra 4 带来 Siri 回顾（Siri Recap）与 Live Rewind 两项音频智能功能。在苹果官方支持页面上，显示上述两项功能适用于 Apple Watch Series 12 和 Apple Watch Ultra 4，目前仅支持英语，且需要 Apple 智能和 Siri AI（Beta 版）。IT 之家此前报道，Siri Recap 定位类似自动化的对话备忘录，通过“环境聆听”（ambient listening），从日常对话中记录概括性信息，帮助用户回顾可能遗漏的事项或重点。而 Live Recap 可显示最近 15 秒实时对话的文字转录，方便用户快速回顾刚才说了什么。此外 Apple Watch 还可监听婴儿哭声、门铃和警笛等重要环境声音。隐私方面，苹果表示，两项功能均不会识别或标注说话者，文字片段和摘要采用端到端加密。原始音频由 S11 芯片的专用硬件隔离区处理后立即删除，不会创建或保存录音。Live Rewind 即使在静音模式下也会发出提示音；Siri Recap 提供的是简要概括，而非逐字记录，并会排除财务信息、政府签发的身份标识等敏感内容。

articles.title: 提速抗癌药物研发：谷歌 Antigravity 上线“AI 炼丹师”，1 小时筛完数千种化合物
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，谷歌 DeepMind 团队昨日（11 月 3 日）发布博文，宣布为 Google Antigravity 推出一套“化学信息学技能”（Cheminformatics Skills），帮助科研人员更快完成药物发现中的文献检索、分子分析、模型构建和新分子设计等工作。IT之家援引博文介绍，在以肺癌药物为例的演示中，AI 智能体可在约一小时内检索数千种化合物、开展匹配分子对分析，并提出具备合成路线的新型刚性大环分子，而类似流程过去往往需要数天。该工具将大语言模型的规划、检索与科学推理能力，与 RDKit 等确定性化学计算工具结合，并接入 ChEMBL 和 PubChem 等公共化学数据库。系统可从论文、专利和产品目录中识别以 IUPAC 名称、马库什结构或 SDF 文件等不同形式出现的同一分子，减少科研人员在数据清洗和格式转换上的时间消耗。在演示中，AI 围绕克唑替尼（crizotinib）与劳拉替尼（Lorlatinib）两类肺癌靶向药展开分析。它检索并整理了 568 个化合物，识别出“分子刚性化”与药效提升之间的关联，随后训练药效预测模型，并设计出多个潜在更优的大环化合物，同时给出反应机理和合成建议。谷歌强调，AI 产出的是“可检验的科研假设”，并非成品药物；受数据稀疏、实验室间检测误差和动态范围限制，所有候选分子仍必须经过合成与实验验证。该功能目前已面向 Google Antigravity 用户开放，企业用户可通过 Google Cloud 账号使用；谷歌还计划向最多 1 万名符合条件的科学家免费提供 6 个月最高用量档位。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，英伟达于 11 月 3 日发布文章称，人工智能正在推动半导体晶圆厂进入“AI 定义工厂”阶段：通过加速仿真、学习型物理模型、AI 智能体和数字孪生，正在显著提速芯片制造中的设计、测试与生产决策。加速仿真（accelerated simulation）指利用 GPU、并行计算、AI 智能体模型等技术，把传统依赖 CPU 的工程仿真从数小时、数天压缩到数分钟甚至毫秒级的过程。在半导体制造中，它让工程师能更快测试工艺方案、预测缺陷风险，而不必先做昂贵且耗时的真实产线实验。IT之家援引博文介绍，随着先进芯片需求上升，制造工艺愈发复杂，良率和工艺质量的容错空间不断缩小。传统产线实验既慢又贵，工程师分析工艺变更、材料反应或缺陷根因，往往需要数天。AI 的价值在于，让工程师在投入真实试验前，先在虚拟环境中更快地比较方案、发现风险。加速仿真的目标是在真实制造之前，更快得到足够可靠的“虚拟实验”结果，从而减少试错、提高良率并降低成本。学习型物理模型（Learned physics models）是指利用机器学习从高精度仿真、实验或产线数据中学习物理规律的模型。它会学习温度、压力、材料、电磁场、等离子体等变量之间的映射关系，从而快速预测复杂物理过程。英伟达在半导体制造报道中，将其视为加速晶圆厂仿真与决策的关键技术之一。数字孪生（Digital Twin）是指在虚拟环境中创建物理对象、系统或流程的动态数字副本。它不只是静态 3D 模型，而是能接收实时或历史数据、模拟运行状态、预测结果，并支持“先在虚拟世界试、再到现实世界做”的决策方式。在英伟达关于半导体制造的报道中，数字孪生被用于构建整座晶圆厂的虚拟模型，帮助工程师在投产前发现瓶颈、验证布局和运营策略。在具体案例中，多物理场仿真软件 COMSOL 借助英伟达 cuDSS，将半导体制造相关仿真速度提升最高 10 倍；西门子则将 cuLitho 集成到 Calibre 光刻软件，关键仿真负载最高提速 17 倍。应用材料公司（Applied Materials）的 Ginestra 平台在集成 cuDSS 后，较仅用 CPU 的方案快最高 10 倍，其 ACE+ 多物理场平台借助 PhysicsNeMo 实现最高 35 倍的形貌仿真加速。AI 还能减少重复仿真。例如，半导体蚀刻中使用的等离子体行为建模复杂、成本高；Lam Research 展示，PhysicsNeMo 可在毫秒级预测等离子体行为，而完整仿真可能需要数天。过去工程师为判断某个芯片制造方案是否可行，需要等待长时间仿真、实验或数据分析；引入 AI 加速仿真、学习型物理模型和 AI 智能体后，许多原本以“天”计的分析任务，可以压缩到“分钟”级完成。英伟达在报道中举例，Advantest 使用 NeMo Switchyard AI 智能体自动选择合适的 AI 模型，把原本需要数小时的任务压缩到数分钟。在先进晶圆厂中，工程师面对的问题往往不是简单查询数据，通常需要判断：某种蚀刻参数是否会损伤晶圆；某个材料或工艺变更是否会影响良率；缺陷究竟来自设备、材料还是工艺条件；多个候选方案中，哪一个最值得投入真实产线验证。传统流程通常要依次进行高精度物理仿真、结果分析、方案比较，有时还要安排实际试验。一次完整仿真可能需要数天，工程师因此难以快速探索大量备选方案。而 AI 可以先帮助工程师缩小范围、发现高风险方案，关键工艺变更仍需要高精度仿真、实验验证和工程师的专业审核。AI 把工程师从“长时间等待计算结果”中解放出来，让他们把时间用于判断、验证和优化；决策链条中的等待时间缩短了，但专业责任和最终把关仍在工程师手中。直观类比是过去像医生要等全套检查报告出来才能初步判断病情；现在 AI 相当于先快速给出多项筛查结果和可能原因，医生可以立刻决定优先做哪些关键检查。速度快了，但最终诊断和治疗决定，仍由医生负责。更重要的是，应用材料公司正基于英伟达 Omniverse 构建整座晶圆厂的数字孪生，可在虚拟环境中模拟物料流动、发现瓶颈并验证布局与运营策略，再决定是否在真实产线落地。应用材料公司利用基于 NVIDIA Omniverse 库构建的数字孪生技术，模拟工厂级布局、吞吐量、成本和工艺控制方面的优化。英伟达称，这一闭环将使工厂从每个生产周期中学习，并更早采取行动；工程师仍负责专业判断与最终决策，但等待答案的时间将大幅减少。利用 NVIDIA Omniverse 库构建的逼真晶圆厂数字孪生模型，用于模拟物料流动、发现瓶颈并在部署前验证运营策略。图片由应用材料公司提供。

articles.title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
articles.content: Sensorized human demonstrations offer scalable data for mobile manipulation, but embodiment differences complicate policy learning. We present Pixel-UMI, a pipeline for learning environment-aware whole-body policies from human data. We first introduce Environment-Aware Retargeting (EAR), which combines reconstructed scene geometry with demonstrated head and gripper trajectories to determine robot posture and generate collision-aware joint and base targets. Delay-calibrated action assignment converts these trajectories into actions. However, kinematic differences can leave residual pose errors, creating viewpoint mismatches between human demonstrations and robot observations. We therefore introduce Retargeting-Error-Aware Masking (REAM), which uses these errors during training to reduce reliance on mismatched views at deployment. Finally, because estimated actions cannot fully capture contact-rich interactions, we collect on-policy human corrections through DAgger to improve performance. We evaluate Pixel-UMI on five challenging tasks spanning articulated-object manipulation, deformable-object handling, constrained-space reaching, whole-body collision avoidance, and contact-rich bimanual coordination, achieving 87.0% average task progress. Video results are available at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel-umi

articles.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
articles.content: General-purpose mobile manipulation requires a combination of capable robot hardware, scalable demonstration collection, expressive whole-body control, and effective policy learning. Yet these components are often developed independently, creating mismatches that limit the capabilities of the complete system. We present Pixel, a co-designed full-stack system for learning general-purpose mobile manipulation. Pixel combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a common policy learning pipeline across human and robot demonstrations. A hierarchical learning stack further enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution. We evaluate the system across hardware, data collection, and policy learning, and demonstrate mobile-manipulation behaviors requiring dexterity, active perception, navigation, and whole-body coordination. We hope that Pixel provides an integrated and extensible foundation for studying how robot hardware, data, control, and learning can be designed together for robot learning. More results at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel

articles.title: EgoActionBench: Benchmarking Dense Action Captioning for Egocentric Human Videos
articles.content: Learning from human data offers a scalable path toward embodied intelligence, yet it requires models to accurately understand fine-grained human actions from egocentric observations. However, existing benchmarks remain limited in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association. We introduce EgoActionBench, a benchmark that represents continuous human manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions associated with the left hand, right hand, or both hands. EgoActionBench contains 1,407 episodes with 41,132 human-refined action annotations. To evaluate such dense predictions, we propose an evaluation protocol that retrieves temporally eligible candidates, selects a prediction by content agreement, and scores semantic fidelity and temporal overlap alongside action precision and recall, jointly capturing what happens, when it happens, and which hand performs it. We benchmark 20 baseline models and systems on EgoActionBench and further adapt two backbones, Qwen3-VL-4B and LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B, through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning on automatically annotated training episodes. EgoAction improves EgoActionScore by 15.9 and 23.2 points on the two backbones, and both adapted models outperform all open-source baselines. Our experiments reveal substantial limitations of current models in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association, highlighting the gap between general video understanding and the action understanding required for embodied intelligence.

articles.title: From Natural Language to Exact Cover: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Zebra Puzzles
articles.content: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation has substantially improved the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) on complex reasoning tasks, including code generation, data analysis, and exam-style question answering. Despite these advances, purely neural LLMs continue to struggle with elementary logical reasoning problems and lack the determinism, soundness, and reliability characteristic of symbolic reasoning systems. Conversely, classical symbolic methods such as SAT solving and exact cover guarantee correctness and completeness, but require problems to be expressed in highly specialized formal encodings, limiting their applicability to natural language inputs. In this work, we present a synergistic neuro-symbolic framework that bridges this gap by combining neural semantic parsing with deterministic exact cover reasoning. Given a Zebra-style logic puzzle in natural language, an LLM translates entities and constraints into structured tool calls that construct an exact cover instance. A symbolic solver then computes the solution and provides feedback to iteratively refine invalid, under- or overconstrained encodings, exploiting the uniqueness property of Zebra puzzles. We conduct a comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple parameter scales, post-training paradigms, and LLM families. The results demonstrate that our hybrid approach consistently outperforms strong plain neural baselines, including CoT prompting, as well as recent neuro-symbolic methods.

articles.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
articles.content: GUI web agents require realistic and interactive environments that remain stable during both evaluation and training. Live website evaluation suffers from changing content, access restrictions, and limited coverage of authenticated workflows, while existing synthetic environments for training often lack functional depth and visual fidelity. We propose WebHarbor, a suite of 153 executable and dockerized website environments that faithfully reconstruct the visual interfaces, content, and functional workflows of real-world web services under deterministic control. We build WebHarbor through task-driven human-agent collaboration, where environments evolve as new tasks expand their functional scope, coding agents implement the required changes, and human contributors audit visual fidelity, functional correctness, and task validity. The resulting suite comprises 3,518 tasks spanning multi-step and post-authentication workflows, where existing works often fail to cover. Beyond reliable evaluation, WebHarbor provides high-fidelity synthetic web environments for cost-efficient reinforcement learning (RL). We demonstrate that a Qwen 4B-level GUI agent trained with RL in WebHarbor generalizes to unseen tasks and performs competitively with leading open-source GUI web agents across four benchmarks. The code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/aiming-lab/WebHarbor.

articles.title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
articles.content: Muon has recently emerged as a promising optimizer for pretraining large language models, offering a speedup over AdamW in minimizing pretraining loss. However, it remains unclear whether Muon's advantage persists after fine-tuning. In this paper, we study the downstream behavior of Muon and AdamW and uncover a surprising trend: beyond a sufficiently large pretraining data budget, AdamW outperforms Muon after fine-tuning. Moreover, as model size increases, AdamW overtakes Muon at progressively smaller pretraining token-parameter ratios. To explain this reversal, we view fine-tuning as a perturbation of the outputs and introduce the margin-to-spread ratio, which measures how far the correct logit lies above the wrong ones relative to how widely the wrong logits are spread. In language models, Muon has the larger margin-to-spread ratio at small data budgets and AdamW at large ones, mirroring the fine-tuning trend. In a linear associative memory, we prove that after one update the margin-to-spread ratio of gradient descent gains on that of Muon as the data budget grows, and simulations show that this trend persists after extended training.

articles.title: Not All Reasoning Generalizes: A Case Study on Learning Generalizable Reasoning Strategies in RLVR
articles.content: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) can enable generalizable improvement for large language model (LLM) reasoning. This paper studies how to incentivize such generalization via reasoning strategies. We study this question with a controllable equation-solving framework: finding multiple inputs x for equations f(x)=y, where f is a non-bijective string function. This setting makes reasoning strategies observable while supporting a clear definition of easy-to-hard out-of-distribution (OOD) shifts, e.g., more solutions, longer y, etc. We uncover a subtle RLVR failure: it teaches the model to solve in-distribution tasks with high accuracy and structured step-by-step derivation, yet under OOD shifts, the same model abandons derivation and collapses to ineffective brute-force enumeration, causing sharp accuracy drops. This observation reveals the deeper challenges of RLVR generalization as it is neither incapable base model nor reward hacking, since the model succeeds in-distribution with the correct reasoning strategy. The key to mitigating this failure is an indirect intervention that surprisingly helps: co-training with bijective inversion tasks. Although these bijective tasks are actually not uniformly harder and even further from the non-bijective OOD evaluation, they make derivation more certain and substantially restore the correct strategy and accuracy under OOD shifts. This effect further motivates our theoretical analysis: outcome-only RLVR can shape reasoning processes through implicitly crediting the effective reasoning strategies more, even without process supervision. To conclude, our analysis framework and findings systematically reveal the crucial role and incentivization of reasoning strategies in RLVR generalization under OOD shifts. Code is available at https://github.com/ziqipang/rl_meta_thinking.

articles.title: Isekai3D SDG: A Platform for Diverse Synthetic Gameplay Visual Data
articles.content: We present Isekai3D Synthetic Data Generation (SDG), a platform for simulating and capturing synthetic 3D gameplay for research in vision and world models, neural graphics, gameplay agents, and other applications. The platform combines reusable environment and character assets with Unreal Engine plugins in a two-stage workflow. First, world simulation generates gameplay while recording the world state, character movements, actions, and camera tracks needed for replay. Second, the recorded simulation is replayed to capture selected outputs, such as rendered video, images, and depth maps, at a specified resolution and frame rate under selected rendering and camera configurations. Separating simulation from capture allows the same recorded gameplay to produce multiple output variants without repeating the original simulation. Visual outputs are accompanied by frame-aligned camera, character, and action metadata. The platform uploads generated data directly in a training-friendly format, reducing intermediate storage, preparation time, and manual processing. This report describes the design of our overall system, including the platform's assets, plugins, and their functionality, explaining how they work together to generate diverse synthetic gameplay data.

articles.title: FADE: Factored Ability--Difficulty Filtering for Online RLVR Scheduling
articles.content: Group-based reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) learns only from prompts whose sampled completions disagree: all-pass and all-fail groups produce zero relative advantage and burn generation budget without moving the policy. Adaptive schedulers try to steer rollouts toward informative prompts, yet they rely on per-prompt pass-rate trackers that entangle two quantities evolving at very different speeds---the policy's shifting competence across reasoning skills and each prompt's intrinsic difficulty. When a single exponential average or Beta counter tracks both at once, short memory scrambles the relative ordering of prompts whereas long memory reports stale pass rates. We introduce FADE (Factored Ability--Difficulty Estimation), a bilinear state-space filter that separates the two timescales. FADE represents each prompt's success logit as the inner product of a whitened $K$-dimensional skill loading with a fast-drifting policy ability vector, minus a slow-shrinking scalar item intercept. articles.content: Communication is important for our well-being, but it can be impaired by disabilities, such as locked-in syndrome (LIS), cerebral palsy (CP), and dysarthria. Non-invasive brain-to-text brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer a promising solution by providing an alternative communication pathway for people with communication disabilities. This is because sentences carry information at such a high level that they can be understood even if some words and letters are missing. However, within sentence-level decoding, sentence classification is not as well investigated as sentence generation, making it difficult to decide whether a sentence should be retrieved or generated in the context of EEG-to-text decoding. articles.title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
articles.content: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) hold promise for zero-shot video task-progress estimation in robot learning, yet existing frameworks frequently suffer from confirmation bias, hallucinating progress in failed executions due to implicit success assumptions or relative temporal ranking designs. Naive prompting of frontier models collapses into a binary success detector that fails to capture nuanced, non-linear progress and failures. While post-training approaches can mitigate this through explicit training, they demand expensive real-world robotics data and require computationally intensive post-training for every individual base model. To resolve these limitations, we introduce D&A (Describe & Assess): our approach decouples progress estimation into an objective, task-grounded textual description of scene dynamics followed by an assessment phase using explicit rubrics. By compelling the VLM to synthesize an explicit, text-based definition of absolute success before scoring, the framework anchors evaluations to an external, global criterion rather than the video's internal timeline. Empirical results demonstrate that our method calibrates zero-shot estimates and mitigates confirmation bias, providing fine-grained, partial progress metrics that accurately penalize failed executions while correctly interpolating successful runs. Being purely prompt-based, D&A generalizes across tasks, embodiments, and benchmarks---matching or surpassing post-trained reward models---and its reward estimates enable efficient downstream reinforcement learning.

articles.title: Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents
articles.content: A model is only half of an AI agent system. The other half is the inference strategy: the reasoning procedure that turns model calls into a response. Today that second half is written by hand, and the experience of building one strategy never carries to the next. We introduce Strategist, a meta-agent that evolves inference strategies across tasks. Each strategy is written as a blueprint,executable code that other strategies can reuse, and together the blueprints form a library. Given a task and a small development set, Strategist retrieves related blueprints, writes candidate strategies, tests them on real samples, and revises them from the results. Every candidate then enters the library, so later tasks build on earlier discoveries. On 30 benchmarks, Strategist beats the strongest baseline on 24 and matches its average accuracy (74.7% vs.74.0%) at 39% lower inference cost. Its strategies also transfer to unseen tasks and other models without further search. The part of an AI system that is not improved on its own now does.

articles.title: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
articles.content: Large language models (LLMs) show growing promise for scientific discovery, yet basic questions remain about what enables reliable discovery. How can we trace the scientific discovery capacity of LLMs to their training data? We study this question as one of missing probability mass and develop a theoretical account in which monofacts-the facts observed once during training-set the discovery capacity. In materials science and regulatory genomics, we directly manipulate monofact rates in training sets and find that more monofacts consistently yield more discoveries across two open-weight model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets. Further experiments show the relationship cannot be explained by training-set diversity alone and can transfer across scientific domains when paired with in-domain data. Together, our results identify monofact rate in training data as a key factor governing discoveries in language models.

articles.title: Benchmark Prediction with Sparse and Unpaired Cached Responses
articles.content: Evaluating a generative model on all queries from all available benchmark tasks is prohibitively expensive. As such, models are often evaluated on different subsets of tasks and/or different subsets of queries from a given task. The resulting collection of responses and the corresponding (model, task) score matrix are sparse and unpaired. In this paper, we introduce the Product Kernel Perspective Space (PKPS), a collection of low-dimensional representations of models based on their embedded responses. PKPS generalizes existing methods for representing black-box generative models by comparing responses to similar -- rather than just identical -- queries and is therefore able to utilize sparse and unpaired information. Theoretically, we show that benchmark prediction using PKPS is query-efficient relative to methods that only use information from dense and paired portions of the evaluation data. Empirically, we show that PKPS-based methods outperform baselines on benchmark prediction across two large benchmark suites.

articles.title: Efficient Closure Learning in Dynamical Systems: A Comparison of Data-Assimilated and Embedded Approaches
articles.content: Increased computing power has transformed computational science and improved predictive capabilities for complex systems, but many phenomena still exceed current simulation capabilities or require rapid evaluations for fast design iterations. Closure models address this challenge by approximating unresolved effects in reduced or incomplete dynamical systems. Data-driven closures offer a flexible mechanism for improving model accuracy and applicability, but approaches that embed the closure within a computational model for construction and training phases can be computationally expensive and cause numerical instabilities in the computational model during training. To avoid the challenges posed by embedded approaches, staged approaches to closure-model learning have been developed. The first stage uses data assimilation to infer state and closure trajectories from observations. The second stage trains a machine learning closure model offline using the assimilated data, thereby avoiding repeated simulator calls during training. In this work, we investigate the cost and accuracy tradeoffs between embedded and staged data-driven closure modeling approaches for a synthetic epidemiological SIQR model with a nonlinear state-dependent quarantine closure. The results illustrate a practical accuracy-efficiency trade-off: for this exemplar, embedded training provides the strongest average accuracy, while the staged approach yields comparable qualitative behavior with a moderate increase in error, substantially fewer model evaluations, and improved optimization robustness.

articles.title: Reviso: Not All Visual Evidence Deserves Equal Attention in Video Captioning
articles.content: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate detailed video captions, yet they may overemphasize minor details while overlooking essential context and key events. We argue that not all visual evidence deserves equal attention, as the importance of visual information depends on the content of each video. Motivated by this observation, we propose Reviso, an agentic video captioning framework that learns what to observe and how to gather relevant visual evidence. From a low-frame-rate global preview, Reviso constructs a hierarchical Context--Focus--Points (CFP) observation plan that identifies the video context, prioritizes key aspects, and defines concrete observation targets and corresponding tools. Guided by this plan, Reviso performs goal-directed active perception by selectively revisiting temporal segments and combining tools for fine-grained inspection. It interprets the acquired evidence, updates its plan as needed, and integrates global and local information to generate the final caption. To learn this observation strategy, we develop a verification-guided pipeline that constructs high-quality training trajectories through factual verification and teacher-guided refinement. We further train Reviso using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), incorporating a key-fact reward for caption quality, a Plan Alignment Reward (PAR) for identifying important observation targets, and an Unproductive Tool-Call Penalty (UTCP) that adjusts observation-cost penalties based on caption quality. Experiments across four video captioning benchmarks show that Reviso outperforms the evaluated open-source baselines, while its generated captions better support downstream video question answering. These findings highlight the effectiveness and potential of priority-guided active observation for video captioning.

articles.title: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
articles.content: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using information about meals, exercise, illness, and glucose measurements. We introduce DiabAgent, a research suite for agentic physiological control comprising the Agentic Physiological Control (APC) framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC controls glucose through medical-device tools, using ongoing observations to infer individual states, accumulate personal experience, and choose treatment actions. We build DiabetSim to simulate different patients, events, and device conditions for scalable virtual testing and training. Using DiabetSim, we construct SweetBench by instantiating 32 scenario designs as 212 glucose-control tasks. With Claude Opus 5.5 and a fixed decision interval of one hour, APC achieves a COGI of 73.5, compared with 71.2 for the open-source closed-loop baseline OpenAPS. Ablations further show that individual adaptation and contextual information improve glucose control. Combining high-frequency rule-based control with lower-frequency agent decisions shows potential for balancing control performance and computational cost. Our work provides a framework, simulator, and evaluation foundation for agents to participate in human physiological control.

articles.title: Four Bridges: Measuring Deception Propensity in a Multi-Agent Game
articles.content: AI agents are increasingly deployed in settings where they interact and coordinate with other agents, yet honesty is mostly measured in single-turn, single-agent benchmarks that pressure the model to deceive. We study deception that emerges in multi-agent interaction without any instruction to deceive. We introduce Kradle, a platform for evaluating AI models, and Four Bridges, an information asymmetry game in which four agents distribute across four rooms: one is the death room, the others hold food worth more if not shared. One agent, the informed agent, knows which room is the death room and can withhold or disclose that information. We evaluate eight frontier models as the informed agent. Deceptive behavior appears in every model and in 73% of all runs (6% to 100% per model), and does not decrease with capability tier within a model family. When the informed agent does disclose, the warning is often challenged, and agents that challenge it enter the death room twice as often as those that do not. Telling all agents that one of them knows the death room collapses deception in six of eight models; telling the informed agent that the room is permanently fatal moves only one. On an open-weight model, an honesty steering vector reduces deception to 0% and adversarial honesty training to 6%. The platform and game provide a testbed for measuring deceptive behavior and comparing interventions.

articles.title: Should We Combine Our Data? Algorithms and Limits for Privately Assessing Data Sharing
articles.content: In this paper, we study when two parties should pool their data to train a machine learning model. Two agents, Alice and Bob, each hold a sensitive labeled dataset and want to train a classifier from a given hypothesis class $\mathcal{H}$. Even when each party's dataset can be perfectly classified on its own, the two parties may follow conflicting labeling standards or have selection biases that affect their features and label sets, such that no single classifier in $\mathcal{H}$ fits their combined data. Before committing to data sharing, Alice and Bob therefore want to test whether a single classifier in $\mathcal{H}$ can jointly fit both datasets---without revealing their individual data points to one another.   We formalize this problem from a learning-theoretic viewpoint via $\operatorname{opt}_\mathcal{H}$, the minimum \emph{number of mistakes} made by any hypothesis in $\mathcal{H}$ on their pooled data. Through interactive communication, the agents must distinguish $\operatorname{opt}_\mathcal{H}=0$ (compatible datasets) from $\operatorname{opt}_\mathcal{H}\geq t$ (conflicting datasets) under pure $\varepsilon$-two-party differential privacy. A trusted curator could do this with $t=O(1/\varepsilon)$, and we ask how small $t$ can be without one. For thresholds on the real line over a domain of size $m$, we show that the optimal $t$ is $\tildeΘ(\log\log m/\varepsilon)$, exponentially smaller than the $Θ(\log m/\varepsilon)$ samples needed to privately learn thresholds, even with a curator. For halfspaces in $\mathbb{R}^d$, the dependence on $m$ jumps to $\log(m)$: we give a protocol with $t=\tilde{O}(d^3\log m/\varepsilon)$ and show that some domains require $t=Ω(d\log(m/d)/\varepsilon)$.

articles.title: Structured Visual Landscape: Generating Preferred Representations in Biological and Artificial Neural Networks
articles.content: Understanding how neurons respond to visual stimulus is an important question in both deep learning and neuroscience. It has significant implications for enhancing the interpretability of black-box artificial neural networks and for understanding the visual representation in the human brain. We propose a structured visual representations landscape and design an activation-based prior that allows us to effectively regularize the landscape with activations from brain regions or neural network units. Our model Vis-Lens integrates a variational autoencoder and a diffusion model into an image generation framework. It enables the generation of natural, realistic preferred images by directly modifying the activation-regularized latent codes without per-image iterative optimization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework on both artificial neural networks and human visual cortex using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data. Our framework improves activation modulation and image realism compared with a recent state-of-the-art method for generating preferred visual representations of these neural targets.

articles.content: We show that the causal structure of spacetime can emerge within the memory of a learning agent performing a quantum information task. articles.content: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD), but most are designed for static geometries and are not equipped to model unsteady flows induced by continuously moving boundaries. articles.title: Evaluating Uncertainty Calibration in Probabilistic Time Series Foundation Models
articles.content: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) are increasingly used for probabilistic forecasting across diverse domains, yet the reliability of their uncertainty estimates remains poorly understood. In this work, we study uncertainty calibration in probabilistic TSFMs from a broader methodological and empirical perspective. We introduce a taxonomy of how TSFMs represent predictive uncertainty and develop a fine-grained evaluation framework for calibration in multi-horizon forecasting that distinguishes pooled, horizon-wise, and stronger conditional notions of calibration. Using this framework, we conduct a comprehensive empirical evaluation of popular TSFMs across diverse datasets and show that current models exhibit distinct and systematic patterns of miscalibration that standard metrics often obscure. We further analyze common post-hoc recalibration methods and characterize which forms of calibration they can improve and which tend to persist. Our results provide practical guidance for evaluating and improving uncertainty calibration in TSFMs and highlight important limitations of current practice.

articles.title: A Scaling Theory of Multi-Epoch Pretraining: Late-Time Overfitting and Ensembling
articles.content: In the near future language model pretraining will become bound by total data rather than total compute. Such a regime requires revisiting scaling laws and scaling law theory. Motivated by prior works that have found utility in ensembling, we study how the number of training epochs and ensemble size jointly shape generalization when training data are fixed. In language-model experiments on FineWeb, logit averaging reduces late-training deterioration, delays optimal stopping, and can outperform wider or deeper single models at matched parameter-token budgets over a common training horizon. To analyze this interaction between data reuse and ensembling, we derive a dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for multi-epoch stochastic gradient descent in power-law random-feature ensembles, tracking error correlations across epochs and models. Ensembling reduces the prediction variance responsible for late-time growth in expected test error, changing the optimal stopping time. We use these stopping times to derive compute-allocation laws at fixed data and individual model sizes. Under this allocation, ensemble size grows with compute at least as fast as training time per member, while excess test loss above the limiting loss decreases as a power of compute.

articles.content: Robust 3D point-cloud recognition is critical for robotics, mapping, and urban sensing, yet point-cloud classifiers often suffer performance drops under domain shifts caused by sensor changes, environmental variation, and acquisition artifacts. Experiments on four corrupted 3D benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines. On ModelNet-40C, 3D-BBDA achieves mean errors of 32.08% (PointNet) and 29.62% (GDANet), outperforming Source-only (35.88% / 34.03%) and BFTT3D (33.78% / 32.36%). 3D-BBDA requires only a single forward pass with no gradient updates making it suitable for real-time, privacy-preserving deployment in transferable 3D recognition pipelines. articles.title: FedReady: Bounded Agents for Federation Formation
articles.content: Federated learning (FL) runtimes standardize aggregation and deployment, but each new study still requires federation formation: selecting task-eligible sites and preparing their local data and task code for federated training or analysis. This preparation recurs when the target changes, while raw records and site-private mappings are excluded from cross-site FL messages. We present FedReady, a system that performs federation formation with bounded LLM agents. Agents propose shared contracts, local adapters, and task code; the runtime owns workflow state and accepts artifacts only after checks tied to their digests. Candidate site discovery prioritizes recall; local eligibility verification checks task support before site admission. Once participating sites and artifacts are fixed, conventional federated training or analysis proceeds without readiness agents. Across 39 simulated retinal sites and four tasks, discovery reaches recall 1.00 at precision 0.65; local eligibility verification removes all 17 false positives without losing an eligible site-task pair. The participating sites supply 45,575 task-record instances and complete four 100-round jobs, including one with a runtime-generated contract. Across ten patient cohorts, preparation supports seven patient populations and holds endpoints at three sources as unsupported. Comparison with manually prepared reference populations and analysis (the manual reference) gives a maximum survival-curve difference of 0.001133. We also analyze 19 development failures, targeted classification ablations, and standalone and heterogeneous agent configurations. These results establish the feasibility of task-specific data preparation before ordinary FL training or analysis.

articles.title: TAMPAgent: Agentic Belief-Space Planning for Mobile Manipulation
articles.content: Open-world robotic mobile manipulation requires acting in physical environments with only partial information. While recent Large Vision-Language Model (LVLM) agents show strong open-world reasoning capabilities, existing architectures that rely on direct tool calling struggle with geometric uncertainty and thus are limited to fully-observable tabletop environments. In contrast, Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) systems can solve long-horizon tasks under partial observability but incur high computational costs and require closed worlds. We endow an LVLM agent with a belief-space planning model operating over an extensible API of perception, planning, and control tools. The agent formulates a partial task plan composed of parameterized observation and execution actions, which is subsequently completed using classical search algorithms. After extracting the plan's geometric constraints, the agent leverages its tool API to bind valid parameter values, satisfying feasibility requirements and producing an executable motion plan. Upon execution, the agent continuously updates its belief history and repeats this closed-loop process by interleaving observation and manipulation actions. Evaluated across complex household mobile manipulation tasks on Rainbow Y1 and Unitree G1 platforms, TAMPAgent significantly outperforms direct tool-calling agentic baselines, demonstrating that integrating TAMP constraint satisfaction into agentic planning loops is essential for unstructured, partially observable environments.

articles.title: Sonar-MoE: In-Backward Expert Updates for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training
articles.content: Most parameters of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model belong to its experts, and standard training keeps every expert gradient in GPU memory until the optimizer step. This memory grows with the number and size of the experts, so it rises as MoE models scale. We introduce Sonar-MoE, which updates each expert tensor during the backward pass and frees its gradient right away. It brings optimizer-in-backward from dense models to batched MoE expert tensors, so the GPU never holds more than one layer of expert gradients. When we fine-tune OLMoE-1B-7B and Granite-3.1-3B-A800M in bf16 with two expert-kernel backends, Sonar-MoE lowers peak memory by 19% to 22%. Its updates are bitwise identical to standard training without expert gradient clipping, and held-out loss stays within 0.003 of all baselines. Each step also takes 17% to 23% less time than standard training with global-norm clipping.
